title: Scott sentences for countable structures
summary: Build countable infinitary descriptions of tuples and use their stabilization to characterize a countable structure up to isomorphism.
abstract: A countable infinitary sentence can say that a set is infinite. A more precise description can identify any given countable structure up to isomorphism among countable structures, provided its language is countable. Starting with the atomic facts about each finite tuple, successive descriptions demand responses to every one-point extension, in both directions. Countable conjunctions allow these tests to continue through countable ordinals until comparisons inside the fixed structure stabilize. One sentence then requires those stable tests throughout a model. Any countable model of that sentence admits a back-and-forth isomorphism with the original structure. The characterization includes finite structures and languages with functions, but can still permit uncountable models of the sentence.

based_on.title: Lectures on Infinitary Model Theory
based_on.pages: Section 2.2, PDF pp. 15–18: ordinal comparison formulas, Lemmas 2.13 and 2.15, and Theorem 2.19
